evals.prompt: Set up licence_audit for local licence and vulnerability checking in my Gleam project. No CI. The root has gleam.toml and a committed manifest.toml, but no licence policy, tool manager, or task runner. Its Gleam compiler supports Git dependencies, OTP 28 is installed, and the project builds for Erlang. I have not decided which licences to allow. Use the latest stable release, pinned after lookup. Produce proposed edits and commands only; do not install tools or make network audit requests.
evals.expected_output: Prefer a Git dev dependency pinned to the verified stable-release commit and run the CLI as a Gleam module. Provide report commands and explain the policy decision still needed for licence enforcement. Do not add a tool manager, invent an allow list, or create CI. Explain the combined gate and report-only exit behavior.
assertions: Selects a verified stable-release commit for a Git dependency in dev_dependencies, preserves the lockfile, and does not assume the package is published on Hex or add a tool manager.
Provides licence and vulnerability reports through gleam run --target erlang -m licence_audit, puts CLI arguments after --, distinguishes reports from check --vulns, and leaves CI unchanged.

Explains that module execution requires compatible Gleam, OTP, Git dependency support, and Erlang compilation, and that the audit includes the added dev dependencies unless production-only coverage is requested.
Leaves licence allow/deny decisions unresolved rather than approving discovered licences or claiming an effective licence gate.

evals.prompt: Add local licence and vulnerability checks in packages/service, without CI changes. Preserve the existing policy and comments. Its gleam.toml contains [tools.licence_audit], allow = ["MIT"], deny = ["GPL-3.0-only"], vuln_severity = "medium", and vuln_block_unknown = true. The project targets JavaScript and uses JavaScript-only FFI that cannot compile for Erlang. The repository uses mise and just; OTP is pinned to 27 for compatibility. A root justfile already has test and check recipes. One locked dependency uses a local path. Produce proposed edits and commands only; do not install tools or make network audit requests.
evals.expected_output: Preserve the policy and OTP pin, use a self-contained executable, and add distinct task names that run in packages/service. Keep the configured vulnerability settings by using check --vulns without overriding flags. Report incomplete source coverage. Do not add CI.
assertions: Preserves the MIT/GPL policy, medium threshold, unknown-severity setting, existing tasks, and OTP 27 pin.
Uses the packages/service working directory for all audit commands and a self-contained binary instead of an OTP-incompatible escript or forcing an Erlang build of the JavaScript-only project.
Provides a combined gate without severity overrides, explains skipped local-path dependencies, and does not add CI.

evals.prompt: Set up local checks and enforce them in GitHub Actions for my Gleam project. It has a committed manifest.toml, an MIT-only audit policy, and mise with OTP 28.3 and a Gleam compiler that supports Git dependencies. The project builds for Erlang and has no existing licence_audit installation. CI already checks out the repo, installs its pinned tools, and downloads dependencies. Keep those steps. Fail for medium-or-higher vulnerabilities and unknown severity. Pin the latest stable licence_audit release and use the same version and policy locally and in CI. Do not add SBOM or notices. Produce proposed edits and commands only; do not install tools or make network audit requests.
evals.expected_output: Merge the two vulnerability settings into the existing policy, pin a Git dev dependency to the verified stable-release commit, reuse existing setup locally and in CI, and run the module with check --vulns without suppressing failure. Do not add a separate CLI install, run interactive update in CI, or replace enforcement with vulns.
assertions: Preserves the MIT policy and sets vuln_severity to medium and vuln_block_unknown to true in one configuration section.

Pins the same verified Git release commit locally and in CI, includes dev dependencies, reuses existing dependency and OTP setup, and runs gleam run --target erlang -m licence_audit -- check --vulns without a separate CLI installation action.
Enforces check --vulns without suppressing failure, interactive update, SBOM, or notices steps.
